$about: 2026-08-06: the two severe repo-shape findings left open by the 2026-08-04 round - SHAPE-03 (a CI workflow file read as a firing PR gate) and SHAPE-06 (no vocabulary for a maintained parallel release branch) - re-run against the current tree before anything was changed, then fixed and re-run after. Both still reproduced, and one of them only partly: half of SHAPE-03's 2026-08-04 evidence had already been closed by the content-hash work on the same date, which the evidence field below states rather than claiming credit for it. The observations keep the 2026-08-04 round's target label so they supersede those findings on the punch list. Every number in an evidence field is from a command executed in this session against the working tree, not from reading a diff.

observations.evidence: Reproduced in two halves, and only one half was still open. (1) CLOSED ALREADY, not by this change: the 2026-08-04 evidence says "the manifest's CI entry passes on file existence". It no longer does - commit e42d39a (2026-08-04, `git log -S'"on.pull_request"'`) gave the `.github/workflows/spec-guard.yml` entry `requiredKeys: ["on.pull_request"]`. Measured: replacing the shipped workflow's trigger with `on: push` makes `node scripts/self-verify.mjs --skeleton` report `drift 1 - 99% adopted (69/70)`, naming the missing key. (2) STILL OPEN, and fixed here: a declared key is not a fired run. With the same workflow carrying `on: pull_request` behind `paths: ['nonexistent-dir/**']` - a trigger that can never match - self-verify reports `drift 0 - 100% adopted (70/70)`. And the assessment method, which is what reads somebody else's repo, had no notion of firing at all: on main, `docs/method/repo-assessment.md` pass 5 detected "Is there a pipeline?" and nothing more. `grep -rn --include='*.md' -e pull_request -e workflow_dispatch -e self-hosted -e paths-ignore docs skills standard`, with `docs/validation/` excluded, returned 2 hits, both incidental - a PR-template filename in the file map and a row in the shipped README - so no method or spec page discussed a workflow trigger at all. Fixed: pass 5 now rates what fires, names the four shapes that carry a workflow and gate nothing (no PR trigger - postgres/openjdk by design; an excluding path/branch filter; disabled at the platform - LibreOffice/core's only PR-triggered workflow auto-closes every PR; a self-hosted runner label with nothing behind it - the repo-specific ones carried from the 2026-08-04 round's observations, not re-verified against those repos here), states the evidence that settles it (`gh run list --workflow <file> --event pull_request`), rates an unprovable gate `partial` at best and never `solid`, says to report "gate execution unverified" the way pass 8 reports a shallow clone, and warns that CI outside the host is still CI. `skills/align-to-standards/onboard.md` carries the same clause in its 8-pass summary, and `docs/method/self-verify.md`'s judgment tier now states self-verify's own limit with the measured path-filter case. What this does NOT close, stated because the 2026-08-04 evidence field bundles it into the same paragraph: a 2-line stub `CONTRIBUTING.md`/`SECURITY.md` still scores as adopted, because those are `fill-from-repo` entries with no content check. That is existence-vs-substance for authored files, not the CI gate this case tests, and it stays open.

Reproduced against the current tree before the change, by the case's own procedure. R23 read "Every PR MUST be based on the mainline, never on another open PR's branch", which makes the pull request carrying a CVE fix to a supported 3.x line non-compliant, because that PR is based on 3.x. The vocabulary gap was total, not partial: `git grep -i -e backport -e 'release branch' -e 'release line' -e 'maintenance branch' main -- ':!docs/validation'` returns nothing - zero occurrences anywhere in the spec, the method docs, the shipped tree or the skills. Fixed as a recorded design act, not a reword: ADR-033 records the decision, the five confirmations behind it (odoo, openssl, dotnet/runtime, FFmpeg, PowerShell) and five rejected forms - leave it out of scope; method-doc guidance with the rules untouched (rejected on SPEC.md's own precedence rule: guidance cannot legalize what a MUST forbids); a new numbered rule (rejected: R23 would go on forbidding what the new rule permitted, and a reader hits R23 first); any long-lived branch as a legal base (rejected: re-opens the stacked-PR failure ADR-026 exists for); and a machine-checkable support matrix in the manifest (rejected for now - a branch existing is not a branch supported, so the check would assert what a checkout cannot show). R23 now bases a PR on the branch it will merge into - the mainline or a declared, protected, never-rewritten maintained release line - binds every one of its own requirements to that line identically, and requires a multi-line fix to land on the mainline first and reach each supported line as its own PR. R18 gains the matching clause: one changelog per line, each with its own `## Unreleased`, the entry written under the heading on the branch the PR targets. `standard/docs/conventions.md` (merged into an adopting repo's AGENTS.md), the decision checklist's branching fork and `docs/method/changelog-process.md` carry it for readers who never open the spec. R25 was deliberately left alone: it is written per release, and a line's version has its own single home on its own branch, which is what R4 asks. Verified after the change: `node standard/scripts/self-verify.mjs --skeleton` reports `drift 0 - 100% adopted (70/70)` with regenerated manifest hashes, and facts-check, spec-structure, decision-records-check, spec-guard --audit, link-check, prose-check, tree-check, file-map --check and site-check all pass. Not closed by this: nothing mechanical enforces the mainline-first ordering or the declared support set - both are review-tier, which ADR-033's confirmation section says outright rather than implying a guard exists.
